name: Jacket structure
description: A fixed steel jacket is a braced tubular, pile-founded substructure that carries the topside and laterally supports and protects well conductors and the pipeline riser; ESDEP states the overwhelming majority of platforms are piled-jacket with steel deck structures. For smaller/marginal fields the read sources describe conductor-supported minimum-facility platforms (MFP/CoSMOS), monopile or caisson alternatives. Appurtenances evidenced on read pages are a clamp-on boat landing (US4679964A, US4932
aliases: Jacket structure (3 or 4-legged steel jacket, or conductor-supported/monopile for smaller fields) with boat landing, riser clamp, barge bump

specifications.metric: Fixed steel jacket (3-/4-legged tubular, — Well conductor size protected by jacket
specifications.basis: ESDEP Lecture 15A.1 section 4.1: jackets "support laterally and protect the 26-30 inch well conductors and the pipeline riser".

specifications.metric: Fixed steel jacket (3-/4-legged tubular, — Typical air gap (topside clearance above maximum wave)
specifications.basis: ESDEP 15A.1 section 2.2: clearance usually taken at approximately 1.50 m, to be increased if reservoir depletion creates significant subsidence.

specifications.metric: Fixed steel jacket (3-/4-legged tubular, — Jacket pile diameter
specifications.basis: ESDEP 15A.1 section 4.2: open-ended tubular steel piles "with diameters up to 2m".

specifications.metric: Fixed steel jacket (3-/4-legged tubular, — Jacket pile penetration, typical
specifications.basis: ESDEP 15A.1 section 4.2: piles driven approximately 40 - 80 m into the seabed.

specifications.metric: Fixed steel jacket (3-/4-legged tubular, — Jacket pile penetration, deep case
specifications.basis: ESDEP 15A.1 section 4.2: "and in some cases 120 m deep into the seabed".

specifications.metric: Fixed steel jacket (3-/4-legged tubular, — Economically feasible water depth, fixed platform
specifications.basis: Wikipedia Fixed platform: "economically feasible for installation in water depths up to about 500 feet (150 m)". Conflicts with the 520 m figure on the Oil platform page; neither preferred.

specifications.metric: Fixed steel jacket (3-/4-legged tubular, — Economically feasible water depth, fixed platform (second source)
specifications.basis: Wikipedia Oil platform: "Fixed platforms are economically feasible for installation in water depths up to about 520 m (1,710 ft)". Conflict noted; neither figure preferred.

specifications.metric: Boat landing / barge impact protection ( — Conductor diameter for clamp-on boat landing
specifications.basis: US4679964A description: conductor pipe "typically in the range of about 26 to about 30 inches in diameter" with wall thickness about one inch; boat landing clamped to it at the water line.

specifications.metric: Boat landing / barge impact protection ( — Example anchor pile length
specifications.basis: US4679964A description: "the piling is 70 feet in length" with about 52 feet protruding into the seabed.

specifications.metric: Boat landing / barge impact protection ( — Clamp-base footprint of prior-art Sea Horse system
specifications.basis: US4932811A background: "The base of the sea horse clamp is approximately forty by forty feet square where piling are driven through the cans".

specifications.metric: Conductor-supported / monopile substruct — Conductor-supported platform water depth applicability
specifications.basis: 2H Minimum Facility Platforms: conductor-supported MFPs "suitable for water depths up to 120m".

specifications.metric: Reliability — Offshore inspection, maintenance and repair share of OPEX
specifications.basis: ESDEP 15A.1 section 9.3: "In the North Sea approximately 20 percent of OPEX are required for offshore inspection, maintenance and repair (IMR)".
ESDEP 15A.1 section 8.1: dynamic analysis performed for system behaviour under wave attack if the natural period exceeds 3 seconds.
